$comment: Ids nobody but the maintainers may list, and prefixes nobody but the maintainers may list under. Three reasons: an id that reads as first-party is an impersonation primitive; the daemon reserves a few names for its own directories; and a panel page's own name — sign-in, moderation, the transparency log — is the first reason again, in the vocabulary of the panel rather than of the daemon (see reserved_note, which also records the eight panel names deliberately NOT here). Removing an entry here is a security change, not a cleanup — and so is ADDING one to either allowlist below. The predicate that reads them is tools/lib/reserved.mjs, imported by both tools/validate.mjs and bot/lib/derive.mjs, so that what CI refuses in the tree and what the bot refuses at ingest cannot be two different answers.
reserved_note: The third reason, added 2026-09-19 and narrowed the same day, is the one whose cost is paid by authors rather than by us, so BOTH halves of it are written down. The panel that replaces this repository's Pages site serves plugin pages under a path, and its own pages — search, sign-in, the transparency log — are pages too. Two different risks were being read as one. ROUTE COLLISION, a stranger's listing served where a panel page is expected: the route scheme already makes that impossible — every non-plugin route lives under /plugins/_/ and no id may begin with an underscore (contract ID-67), and today's Pages site keeps plugin pages under /p/ for the same reason — so a reservation buys nothing against it, and sixteen of them bought nothing against the next route the panel invents. IMPERSONATION, a name that makes a user believe Astra, or the machinery it asks them to trust, is the one speaking: no URL scheme touches that, and it is the only one of the two risks a reserved id is a control for. So the panel names kept below are the ones that name a part of Astra or of its trust apparatus — sign-in and the account, publishing, moderation, the transparency log, the author records, the API — and EIGHT WERE RELEASED DELIBERATELY rather than left out by oversight: about, docs, feed, help, new, rss, search, sitemap. Each of those is an ordinary English word a real author may reasonably want for a real plugin, and none of them claims to be us; re-adding one is a policy change and needs the argument this note did not make for it. The two close calls, recorded so they are not re-fought: `publish` could honestly belong to a plugin about publishing something and is kept anyway, because the registry's publish flow is where an author is told about signing keys and binding tokens, so a listing under that name is a ready-made instruction to hand them over; `search` is the panel's busiest page and is released anyway, because searching mediates no trust, and if /search is ever shadowed it will be because ID-67 was relaxed, which is the panel's router to catch and not this file. Releasing is not free either — an id belongs to the first release published under it, so a name given back is given back into a race — and that is the trade taken with the eyes open: the names kept are the ones no honest author is deprived of. WHICH names are reserved for the panel, WHICH were released, and that the first are refused while the second actually validate, are asserted in tools/selftest/validation.mjs rather than restated as a second list here — a list in prose beside the list it describes is the one that goes stale. astra stays first below; the rest are sorted.
first_party_repos_note: KNICE-TECH/astra-chess is here ONLY so the frozen astra-chess listing, whose source.repo and signed version files still name it, keeps validating. The owner login KNICE-TECH is no longer first-party: the organisation was renamed MINICE-AI on or before 2026-09-12, and GitHub frees a renamed login for anybody to register. The entry grants that one repository name nothing that reaches a user: plugins/astra-chess is unlisted, a release cannot lift unlisted (bot/lib/derive.mjs), and E_TRADEMARK refuses any astra- release from a KNICE-TECH repository (bot/policy/trademarks.json). tools/selftest.mjs fails if any listing under a KNICE-TECH repo pair is not unlisted. Delete the entry when astra-chess moves to MINICE-AI/astra-chess.
first_party_owners_note: Owner logins whose EVERY repository may list under a reserved prefix — present and future, including one a collaborator with push access creates. Wider than first_party_repos by construction, so an entry here is a statement that the project vouches for the whole account. MINICE-AI is the organisation named KNICE-TECH until its rename; KNICE is Astra team (publishers/KnlCE.json) and astra-chess is his. The old login is deliberately NOT here: a renamed login is free for anybody to register, so trusting it would hand every astra- id to whoever registers it first.
staging_listing_id_note: MOD-16's path-test listing, and the one id in this file that is reserved by being USED rather than by being refused. The estate needs a listing it can delist, relist, revoke and un-revoke on demand — to walk a withdrawal end to end, to drill the alarm, to give TRUST-26's takedown bound something to count that is not somebody's plugin — and doing that to a stranger's listing is not an option. So one id is set aside for it. The member is spelled `staging_listing_id` rather than added to `reserved` above, because the two lists mean opposite things: `reserved` is a name nobody may list under, and this is a name exactly one listing WILL be published under. Three rules read it and they are the whole of the reservation: bot/lib/derive.mjs derives it `unlisted: true` on its FIRST listing, before any plugin.json exists, so it is never in a signed catalogue for the interval between a publish commit and a delist commit; tools/validate.mjs refuses the listing on the tree if it is not unlisted; and tools/selftest/validation.mjs asserts both, plus that the repository this listing comes from does not quietly become a second publisher. The value is the registry plan's own (§1.2, M-T2.1) and the contract's token file still records it as pending (§1.3 row 6) — a pending RE-VALUE, not a pending decision: when the token file catches up it records this string. `astra-` is a reserved prefix, so the owner of the publishing repository must be mihailinl or MINICE-AI, which bot/policy/trademarks.json's allow_repo_owners also requires for the `astra` mark. Spelled here once and read through tools/lib/reserved.mjs's stagingListingId(); nothing may copy the literal.
